title: Design a Food Rating System
statement:
Build a class `FoodRatings` that tracks the ratings of a fixed menu of foods, each belonging to one cuisine, and can report the best food of a cuisine.

- `FoodRatings(foods, cuisines, ratings)` loads `n` foods: food `foods[i]` belongs to cuisine `cuisines[i]` and starts with rating `ratings[i]`. All three arrays have length `n`, and food names are all different.
- `changeRating(food, newRating)` sets the rating of the food named `food` to `newRating`. Its cuisine never changes.
- `highestRated(cuisine)` returns the name of the food in `cuisine` whose current rating is largest. When several foods share that rating, return the name that comes first in dictionary (lexicographic) order, where a proper prefix comes before any longer string that starts with it.

`changeRating` is only called with a food on the menu, and `highestRated` only with a cuisine that has at least one food.
constraints: foods[i] and cuisines[i] contain only lowercase English letters
All names in foods are distinct
changeRating is called only with a food in the system
highestRated is called only with a cuisine of at least one food
At most 2 * 10^4 calls in total are made to changeRating and highestRated

signature.name: FoodRatings
signature.constructor: FoodRatings(String[] foods, String[] cuisines, int[] ratings)

notes:
## Intuition

Scanning every food of a cuisine on each `highestRated` call costs O(n) per query. A heap per cuisine, ordered by rating (high first) and then by name, puts the answer on top. The difficulty is `changeRating`: removing an arbitrary entry from a heap is awkward. Instead, push a fresh `[newRating, food]` entry and leave the old one in place. A map keeps every food's true rating, so an entry whose rating no longer matches is *stale*, and `highestRated` simply pops stale entries off the top until a live one appears.

## Approach

1. In the constructor, record each food's `rating` and its cuisine in `cuisineOf`, create a heap for each new cuisine in `heaps`, and push `[rating, food]` into its cuisine's heap.
2. `changeRating`: update `rating` and push `[newRating, food]` into the food's cuisine heap.
3. `highestRated`: while the top entry's rating differs from `rating.get(food)`, `pop` it. Return the top food's name.
4. `before(a, b)` defines the heap order: higher rating first, and for equal ratings the smaller name first.
5. `push` sifts a new entry up; `pop` moves the last entry to the root and sifts it down.

## Example 1, step by step

The korean heap holds `[9, "kimchi"]` and `[7, "bulgogi"]`, so `highestRated("korean")` returns `"kimchi"`. The japanese heap's top is `[14, "ramen"]`, which is live, so the answer is `"ramen"`. `changeRating("sushi", 16)` pushes `[16, "sushi"]`, which rises to the top: `"sushi"`. `changeRating("ramen", 16)` pushes `[16, "ramen"]`; it ties with sushi on rating but `"ramen" < "sushi"`, so it becomes the top and the last query returns `"ramen"`. The stale `[14, "ramen"]` and `[8, "sushi"]` stay buried until they surface.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) to build; O(log(n + c)) for `changeRating`; amortized O(log(n + c)) for `highestRated`, where c is the number of calls, since each entry is popped at most once.
- Space: O(n + c): one heap entry per food plus one per rating change.

## Pitfalls

- Break ties by name, smaller first: a heap ordered on rating alone returns an arbitrary food among equals.
- An entry is stale when its rating differs from the map, not when the food has "changed": a food changed back to an old rating makes an old entry valid again, which is harmless because it names the right food with the right rating.
- Look the cuisine up from the food in `changeRating`; the call does not pass it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rating` | map from each food to its current rating |
| `cuisineOf` | map from each food to its cuisine |
| `heaps` | map from each cuisine to its heap of `[rating, food]` entries |
| `heap` | the heap of the cuisine being queried |
| `before` | true when entry `a` should sit above entry `b` |
| `index`, `parent`, `left`, `right`, `best` | positions used while sifting a heap |

narration.3: Map each food to its current rating: the truth every heap entry is checked against.
narration.4: Remember each food's cuisine so changeRating can find the right heap.
narration.5: One heap per cuisine, keyed by the cuisine's name.
narration.9: The first food of a cuisine creates that cuisine's empty heap.
narration.12: Push the food's starting entry into its cuisine's heap.
narration.17: Record the new rating; any older entry for this food becomes stale.
narration.18: Push a fresh entry instead of hunting for the old one inside the heap.
narration.23: Does the top entry's rating disagree with the food's current rating? Then it is stale.
narration.24: Discard the stale entry and look at the new top.
narration.26: The top is live: the highest rating, with the smallest name among ties.
narration.30: A higher rating sits higher; on equal ratings the lexicographically smaller name does.
narration.38: Stop sifting up once the entry no longer beats its parent.
narration.53: Pick whichever child should sit above the current entry...
narration.55: Neither child beats it, so the entry has found its place.
